newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pare record gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares pare record gains in late trade.

text.p: German shares came off highs in afternoon electronic trade, as the market ran out of steam somewhat, following the record-breaking rally of earlier in the session.
By 1344 GMT the IBIS DAX index stood at 3,655.49 points, down 13.82 points or 0.38 percent, while June DAX futures were down 18 points at 3,662.5 points.

"We've seen as much buying as selling lately -- in fact we're net sellers at the moment. There seems to be a lot of derivatives interest around which is driving gains," said one German equities trader.

Dealers said the rally petered out mainly because of the absence of new data to drive the market past the psychologically key 3,700 point level, although one dealer said that such a breach was on the cards in the near future.
"We may not see 3,700 today, but that is not the end of it," said a Stuttgart dealer. "I am confident we can make it there."

Among the big losers in afternoon trade was the telecoms group Deutsche Telekom, which fell sharply after Bonn sources were reported as saying that the government planned to sell 287 million Telekom shares in 1997.
Telekom shares fell 1.30 marks, or 3.25 percent, at 38.75 marks in afternoon IBIS electronic trade.
The sources were also reported as saying that the German government was considering the sale of its remaining stake in Telekom by the end of 1998.

German Posts and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch said earlier that Bonn would sell off Telekom shares faster than planned to help cut borrowing and qualify for European economic and monetary union.
Among the growth engines over the day were steel group Thyssen AG and retailer Metro AG.
Metro was up 6.70 marks, or 3.77 percent, at 184.20 marks after reporting its first group profit on ordinary activiites of 1.1 billion marks.
Thyssen, meanwhile, was off earlier highs at 399.10 marks, a rise of 5.60 marks, having earlier hit a high of 404 marks after announcing an 81 percent increase in first-half pre-tax profit.
